text: When the Inspector examined the ground a hundred yards round the hollow
why: In ¶108 the Inspector says he has examined the ground for a hundred yards in each direction.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow?
why: The horse is known to have been in the hollow (¶37) and has vanished, and Holmes is searching for tracks, so the question follows naturally.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — tracks lie beyond the ground searched, or the search missed them
id: q.horse_tracks=tracks lie beyond the ground searched, or the search missed them
why: Holmes keeps searching after the Inspector's claim, and the Inspector has just admitted missing the vesta, so a missed or more distant trail is a natural thought.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — led away over ground that takes no prints
id: q.horse_tracks=led away over ground that takes no prints
why: This is a plain explanation for finding no tracks on moorland, and it reveals nothing specific.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — towards Mapleton
why: Mapleton is the nearby rival stable with an interest in the favourite's disappearance (¶66), so a reader has reason to consider it.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — back towards King's Pyland
why: A loose horse returning to its home stable is an obvious general possibility, since the hollow is near King's Pyland.
